newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to end rating rules on overseas bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to end rating rules on overseas bond issues.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Friday it would abolish from next week credit rating requirements for overseas issues of straight bonds.
The ministry said companies would be allowed to issue the non equity-linked bonds abroad if the funds raised were used to import capital goods.

Companies seeking to issue such overseas bonds are currently required to obtain an international credit rating higher than BBB. The ministry also said payments on deferred imports by small- and medium-sized companies would be expanded to 180 days from the current 150 days if the imports were for re-export to neighbouring countries.
The ministry earlier said ceilings on equity-linked bond issues overseas would be lifted.
The ministry said equity-bond ceilings were raised to 50 percent of the total share capital on April 1 from 15 percent and would be completely lifted from next week.
Overseas issues of equity-linked bonds, including convertible bonds and depositary receipts, totalled $2.04 billion in 1996. --Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5645
